chunks: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ayyashi from Ja'far ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu'awiya said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who stood in the obligatory prayer and made a mistake, thinking it was a voluntary prayer, or was in the voluntary prayer and thought it was obligatory. He said: 'It is whatever prayer he began with.'
ai.seo_question: How to determine if a prayer is obligatory or voluntary when there is doubt about the intention?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, clarifies the jurisprudential rule of 'al-ibtida' (initial assumption) in cases of doubt during prayer. It establishes that the legal status of the prayer—whether obligatory (fard) or voluntary (nafl)—is determined by the intention held at the moment of commencement, providing a practical solution for worshippers experiencing uncertainty. This principle underscores the Shia emphasis on intention (niyyah) as the foundational element that defines the nature of the act of worship.
